newsitem.title: UK: Food aid shipments forecast at 7 mln T in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Food aid shipments forecast at 7 mln T in 1996/97.

text.p: Food aid shipments to poor nations are forecast to reach seven million tonnes in the 1996/97 (July/June) harvest season, exceeding minimum requirements, the International Grains Council (IGC) said on Wednesday.

The IGC's Food Aid Committee which met on Monday to review progress of grain aid forecast total shipments to exceed by 1.6 million tonnes the minimum obligations agreed under its 1995 Food Aid Convention.

An IGC statement said the Committee also focused on the increasing role of triangular transactions and local purchases in recent years. In 1995, such forms of food aid were estimated to have reached 1.3 million tonnes.
Another focal point of discussion was possible changes in donor food aid policies in the wake of the recent World Food Summit in Rome and the forthcoming WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore.

"It was noted that significantly lower prices which have been prevailing on grain markets in recent months would help to reduce pressures on the food import bills of developing countries," said the IGC.
